reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis relies on a speculative dual mechanism (M–N bond strengthening and Pt-rich shell formation) from a single N-doping/etching treatment on a complex multi-principal-element alloy, without clear thermodynamic or kinetic justification for selective Pt segregation or stability under oxidizing exhaust conditions.
reasons.testability: The proposed falsification test is well-defined with clear metrics (activity retention, Pt dissolution) and a quantitative threshold (15–20% improvement), making the hypothesis decisively testable.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a critical problem (PGM stability in transient exhaust) with a novel, single-step intervention, but its low scientific plausibility and high uncertainty make it a risky starting point for a researcher.
